caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 175 of 2009
lawyer:
Dr. A.K.M. Ali, Advocate, instructed by Muhammad Nawab Ali, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
For Respondents ------ Not represented
parties:
Securities and Exchange Commission represented by its Chairman ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Dona Securities Chamber Building (2nd floor) 122-124, Motijheel C/A, Dhaka and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 11.11.2007 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3280 of 2002 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The relevant facts of the case, in brief, are that a petition of complaint was filed by the Securities and Exchange Commission, represented by the Executive Director in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka stating that the accused firm and other accused acted as dealer / broker in the Dhaka Stock Exchange and in such capacity of being dealer / broker was involved in fraudulent activities during the month of July to December, 1996 within the mischief of Section 17 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1996. The offence was detected by an inquiry committee formed by the Securities and Exchange Commissioner who inquired into the matter under section 21 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969. In the complaint petition it has been further stated that according to the inquiry report dated 27.03.1997 it appears that the accused being dealer / broker committed offence described in section 17 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969 and as such it is liable for punishment under Section 24 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance 1969. In the complaint petition it has also quoted the report of the inquiry committee which is as follows: "They are one of the major traders in DSE concentrating mainly in the share of Shine Pukur Holding Share. They were both buyer and seller. Most of their trading volume was with Beximco Associates sponsors. Their total trading amounts to Tk. 124.66 crore out of which DVP transaction is Tk. 37.72 crore, the general impression is that they played a role in market operations relating to Shine Pukur Shares both within and outside DSE. This firm acted on unsigned orders given by Satkhira Fisheries for sale of share of Shine Pukur Holding Ltd. The dealings of the firm indicate manipulation within the meaning of Section 17 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance, 1969". The Magistrate took cognizance under section 25 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance. The accused A.K.M. Shamsudohha appeared before the High Court Division and obtained ad-interim anticipatory bail. The case was then transferred to the Court of Sessions Judge, Dhaka and at the time of hearing of discharge application under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the case was then transferred to the Metropolitan Sessions Judge, Dhaka being Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 560 of 1999. It was then transferred to the Court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka, for trial and after hearing the petition under section 265C of the Code of Criminal Procedure the Court rejected the application by an order on 27.05.2001 and fixed 11.06.2001 as the date for framing of charge. The trial Court on 20.06.2001 framed charge against the petitioner under section 17(e) (ii) (v) read with section 24 of the Securities and Exchange Ordinance. 

 3. The respondents herein filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 3280 of 2002 under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure seeking quashment of the proceeding of C.R. Case No.1075 of 1997 under sections 17 and 24 of the Securities Exchange Ordinance, 1969 which was subsequently renumbered as Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 560 of 1999 which was then pending in the Court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka. 

 5. After hearing the parties, by the impugned judgment and order, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute and quashed the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 1075 of 1997 under sections 17 and 24 of the Securities Exchange Ordinance, 1969, pending in the Court of Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka as Metropolitan Sessions Case No. 560 of 1999. 

 7. Dr. A. K. M. Ali, the learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that the Inquiry Committee detected irregularities in the Trading of the Respondent Company which indicated manipulated trading and as such without taking further evidence and deposition during the trial the matter cannot be decided and the High Court Division erred in quashing the criminal proceeding. The learned Counsel further submits that similar cases were previously brought before this Division in which by judgment reported in 50 DLR (AD) 189 and 55 DLR (AD) 47, this Division held that there was prima face allegation of contravention of section 17 of the Ordinance in the complaint petition and as such the proceeding could not be quashed at that stage. Hence, the learned Counsel submits that the judgment of the High Court Division quashing the proceeding cannot be sustained in law. 

 II. For that while disposing the application under Section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure under the facts and circumstances of the present case the High Court Division traveled beyond its jurisdiction, therefore the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law;
